positive_patterns.title: Deck narrative shared DNA
positive_patterns.text: # Deck Commonality Notes ## Shared DNA / Stage-by-Stage (verbatim) Shared DNA across strong fundraising pitches: - Lead with immediate clarity: what you do, for whom, and why now. - Make the problem economically explicit: who pays for pain and what it costs. - Show mechanism before magic: explain how the product creates the outcome. - Replace adjectives with proof: named metrics, timeframe, and denominator. - Demonstrate wedge first: specific beachhead, then expansion path. - Differentiate ag...

anti_patterns.label: jargon_overload
anti_patterns.description: High buzzword density with weak operational specificity and unclear claim support.

anti_patterns.label: no_ask
anti_patterns.description: Missing explicit raise ask or disconnected use-of-funds plan.

anti_patterns.label: no_proof
anti_patterns.description: Claims with weak or missing measurable proof points.

anti_patterns.label: tam_only
anti_patterns.description: TAM-heavy framing without traction, GTM, or customer evidence.

anti_patterns.label: slide_overload
anti_patterns.description: Narrative overwhelmed by excessive slide references or dense structure.

anti_patterns.label: no_demo
anti_patterns.description: No working demo, prototype, or live product shown in hackathon pitch.

anti_patterns.label: no_theme_alignment
anti_patterns.description: No explicit connection to hackathon theme or challenge prompt.

anti_patterns.label: slides_only
anti_patterns.description: Presentation is slides-only without live demo or working product evidence.

anti_patterns.label: too_many_features
anti_patterns.description: Feature listing without depth on any single innovation.

anti_patterns.label: no_cta
anti_patterns.description: No clear call-to-action at the end of the hackathon pitch.

anti_patterns.label: no_results
anti_patterns.description: Missing results or findings section in final year project presentation.

anti_patterns.label: no_evaluation
anti_patterns.description: No evaluation methodology, testing, or benchmarking presented.

anti_patterns.label: unsupported_claims
anti_patterns.description: Qualitative claims without quantitative evidence or baseline comparisons.

anti_patterns.label: missing_methodology
anti_patterns.description: No clear methodology, approach, or implementation description presented.

pre_seed: Show a narrow wedge and clear early user profile.
Anchor claims with concrete pilot or demand proof.
seed: Show repeatability in acquisition or retention.
series_a: Present growth mechanics and unit economics together.
Tie funding to execution milestones and hiring plan.
series_b: Show operating leverage and category strategy.
Provide benchmarked scale economics and expansion plan.
university_hack: Show a working demo within the first minute.
Explain how your hack aligns with the event theme.
Focus on one core innovation with technical depth.
End with a clear call-to-action for judges.
corporate_hack: Demonstrate alignment with sponsor problem statement.
Show feasibility and potential for real-world deployment.
Focus on practical implementation over theoretical design.
web3_hack: Show on-chain demo or protocol interaction.
Explain UX improvements for non-crypto users.
Demonstrate smart contract or protocol innovation.
science_hack: Show scientific rigor in approach and measurement.
Demonstrate measurable impact on the target problem.
Explain data collection and analysis methodology.

common_failures: Do not hide what you build until late in the pitch.
Do not rely on buzzwords instead of concrete outcomes.
Do not spend too long on problem setup before solution clarity.
Do not end without a memorable close and explicit ask.
Do not present TAM without execution evidence.
Do not let slides dominate the narrative.

do_rules: Lead with a clear one-liner before details.
Tell a coherent story with simple language and concrete proof.
Show traction with numbers tied to a timeframe.
Explain the business model in plain terms.
Close with a specific ask and milestone plan.
Prioritize what investors must remember after the pitch ends.
Focus on narrative. The rest is commentary. (see footnote)
Keep your presentation smooth by narrating the story behind your slides; not the opposite.
Lead with one traction metric before describing broad market upside.
State exactly what you are raising and which milestones it funds.
Use plain claims first, then add one proof datapoint per claim.
dont_rules: Do not hide what you build until late in the pitch.
Do not rely on buzzwords instead of concrete outcomes.
Do not spend too long on problem setup before solution clarity.
Do not end without a memorable close and explicit ask.
Do not present TAM without execution evidence.
Do not let slides dominate the narrative.

structure: Use problem -> solution -> proof -> ask in that order.
Open with what you do, for whom, and why now in one sentence.
Tie the close to amount raised, runway, and concrete milestones.
Do not spend early time on background before the core value claim.
clarity: Replace jargon with plain language and concrete nouns.
Keep each sentence focused on one investor-relevant point.
Avoid acronyms unless they are investor-standard terms.
Trim adjectives that are not backed by evidence.
evidence: Attach a metric, timeframe, and denominator to major claims.
Name customer type or cohort when citing traction numbers.
Show baseline vs current to prove movement over time.
Use one strong datapoint instead of multiple weak claims.
market: Define beachhead ICP before broad TAM expansion narrative.
Name alternatives and explain your specific wedge advantage.
Show why timing is favorable now with execution signal.
Avoid TAM-only framing without GTM or traction proof.
delivery: Keep pace steady and pause before key proof statements.
Remove filler words from opening and close first.
Avoid repeating the same phrase across adjacent sentences.
Use short transitions between beats to reduce verbal drift.

anti_pattern_playbook.no_proof: Replace one abstract claim with one metric + timeframe + denominator.
anti_pattern_playbook.no_ask: State raise amount, runway months, and 2-3 milestones funded.
anti_pattern_playbook.tam_only: Follow TAM with ICP wedge, GTM motion, and proof of execution.
anti_pattern_playbook.jargon_overload: Swap buzzwords for plain actions and measurable outcomes.
anti_pattern_playbook.slide_overload: Tell spoken narrative first; slides should only support key proof.
